rows.notes: The document is explicitly a review report ('Review paper: Pests, diseases and invasive species', CABI, June 2022) synthesising literature on Earth Observation for pest and disease management under climate change. Its only own activities are a stakeholder workshop (Tables 3 and 6), bibliometric searches of Web of Science/CABDirect (Figure 1, Table 7), and brief mention of pilot work on irrigation datasets and a M. acridum efficacy map; none of these constitute primary data on remote-sensing early stress detection reducing prophylactic pesticide use. On the claim topic the review only summarises other studies (e.g. Poblete et al. 2020, Raza et al. 2020, Hornero et al. 2020, Zhang et al. 2016) on detection of disease or pest damage; it states that detection often comes too late for in-season action and nowhere reports a measured reduction in pesticide applications attributable to spectral/thermal sensing. Even if treated as primary, the material supports only the detection precondition, not pesticide reduction (upstream).

notes: Full text appears complete (including annexes). The study is a literature/strategy review with stakeholder consultation, not a primary study; all questions answered 'no' per rule 3.
